answer: Cross-Epoch Consistency Ledger. Each identity must, per epoch, reach a random consistency summit of behavioural checks: task intervals, peer overlap, and timing entropy. Deviation beyond a learned threshold for two consecutive epochs freezes rewards. An attacker cloning identities must sustain these correlated patterns across many epochs; each maintained clone costs continuous compute and attention, while a whisper of shared timing correlation flags the whole cohort. Consistency failures compound, so a sonnet of stable behaviour is cheaper than mass fakery.
